walkthroughs.body_html:
Only about 10% of energy passes from one trophic level to the next.

The rest is lost as heat (respiration), in movement, and in waste (faeces, urine).

That's why pyramids of biomass narrow towards the top — there's less energy to support fewer top predators. 🌿

Example: 10000 J in grass → 1000 J in rabbit → 100 J in fox.

To estimate plant populations: place quadrats randomly, count organisms inside, work out the mean per quadrat, then scale up.

Total = mean per quadrat × (total area ÷ quadrat area)

Example: mean of 5 daisies per 1 m² quadrat, field is 200 m² → estimate 1000 daisies.

Random placement avoids bias.

To estimate animal populations, use the Lincoln–Petersen formula:

N = (M × C) ÷ R

M = number first marked and released. C = number captured on second visit. R = number recaptured with marks.

Example: mark 20, recapture 25 of which 5 are marked → N = (20 × 25) ÷ 5 = 100.
